ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A digital baseband transmission system has the transmission characteristics shown in the figure. Given that \(f_1 = 10.8\) MHz and \(f_2 = 18\) MHz, the bandwidth efficiency is ________ Baud/Hz.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the figure is a curve of the baseband transmission characteristic H(f) with respect to frequency f, with a shape that is a trapezoidal low-pass characteristic symmetric about the vertical axis; between -f1 and f1 the amplitude remains flat, and the height is labeled as 1; from f1 to f2 and from -f1 to -f2 are linear roll-off transition bands; after |f| exceeds f2 it is zero. Then reason: according to the Nyquist raised-cosine edge relationship, the symbol rate Rs = f1 + f2. Substituting f1 = 10.8 MHz and f2 = 18 MHz gives Rs = 10.8 + 18 = 28.8 MBaud. The single-sided baseband bandwidth B in the figure is f2 = 18 MHz. Therefore the bandwidth efficiency eta = Rs / B = 28.8 / 18 = 1.6 Baud/Hz.

raw_record.question_text: A digital baseband transmission system has the transmission characteristics shown in the figure. Given that \(f_1 = 10.8\) MHz and \(f_2 = 18\) MHz, the bandwidth efficiency is ________ Baud/Hz.

method.method_draft: First describe the plotted transmission characteristic: a symmetric trapezoidal low-pass H(f), flat between -f1 and f1 and zero beyond ±f2. Use the Nyquist raised-cosine edge relation Rs=f1+f2. Substitute f1=10.8 MHz and f2=18 MHz to get Rs=28.8 MBaud. The one-sided baseband bandwidth shown is B=f2=18 MHz. Therefore eta=Rs/B=28.8/18=1.6 Baud/Hz.

method.method_draft: Identify the plotted characteristic as a raised-cosine/Nyquist baseband response. Compute the roll-off factor from the two labeled edges: alpha=(18-10.8)/(18+10.8)=7.2/28.8=0.25.
